tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height. Add wall_height_ft to estimates (migration). TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php currently drops geometry — preserve meta.perimeter. prep.what: Add wall height as a project-level setting, stop the seeder from dropping room perimeter, and emit wall paint SF (perimeter × height) as a line item per room.
prep.understand: The takeoff engine returns floor area and room perimeter from 2D geometry. Wall height is the missing third dimension — it must come from user input. TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php currently calls the engine, maps measurements to line items, and silently drops geometry.rings and meta.perimeter. Without perimeter, wall area cannot be computed. CT Pros' primary trade is painting — this is the most important missing calculation in the entire takeoff flow.

In TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php, find where it processes room data from the engine response. Extract meta.perimeter alongside meta.area and room_name — stop dropping it

Compute wall_paint_sqft = meta_perimeter * estimate->wall_height_ft per room. Emit a line item: kind='area', surface='wall_paint', unit='sqft', quantity=wall_paint_sqft, description='Wall paint — {room_name}'
Add a wall_height_ft number input (default 8) to the Takeoff Vue UI or estimate form. Wire it to the estimate model
Write a seeder unit test: given room with meta.perimeter=40 and wall_height_ft=8, assert output has quantity=320 and surface='wall_paint'
Run php artisan test to verify no regressions

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Harborview demo: rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text (55 live words, zero room labels). Holabird proves the live-text lane works (92/109 named). v2 = productize the M3 tiles spike as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' + callout-vs-room noise filter.

prep.what: Productize the M3 tiles spike into an opt-in AI label-reading action for firms that outline all text, and add a noise filter to strip callout annotations from room name matches.
prep.understand: The free live-text lane finds zero room labels when PDFTron outlines text — it returns 55 morphological words but none are room names (Harborview case). The M3 tiles spike (run_labels_m3tiles.py) tiles the PDF into image chunks, sends each to MiniMax vision, and merges labels back onto room polygons by centroid proximity. It runs ~4.3 min/sheet and costs money, so it must be opt-in behind a §7a metered-credits event. Separately, Holabird's live-text lane picks up 'UP' (stair), 'FEC', and multi-word general notes alongside room names — the callout filter is the quality improvement.
approach: Read docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py: understand tiling parameters (tile size, overlap), how MiniMax is called, and how label results are merged back to room polygons by centroid proximity

Design the productization hook: gate AI label-reading behind an explicit opt-in button in the UI that fires a §7a metered-credits event before calling the service route. The route accepts project_id, triggers the M3 tiles pipeline, and returns labeled room results for the React review UI
Plan the MINIMAX_AI key placement: add to VPS .env following the existing secrets pattern in docs/README-SERVICE.md

Build the callout-vs-room classifier: stair annotations = short all-caps with cardinal directions ('UP', 'DN'); equipment codes = alphanumeric with dashes ('FEC', 'AHU-1'); general notes = contains punctuation or >3 words; valid room names = 1–3 capitalized words. Apply post-MiniMax before persisting labels
Wire into a new service route (opt-in only) and validate against Harborview — target >0 named rooms where it currently returns 0

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: engine/assemblies.py scaffolded (assemblies-lite). Full version = room classification → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Extend the assemblies engine to map each room classification to a full set of trade quantities (floor SF, wall paint SF, LF baseboard) using wall height and CSI formulas, then emit them as rows in the export Excel.
prep.understand: engine/assemblies.py has a scaffold from assemblies-lite. A full assembly ties a room classification (e.g. 'bedroom', 'corridor', 'bathroom') to assembly specs — each spec names a trade, a quantity formula (floor_sf * 1.1 for flooring with 10% waste; perimeter * height for wall paint; perimeter for baseboard LF), and a CSI division. Wall height is not in the PDF; it comes from a project default or hard default (8 ft). The Excel export (build_sheet_takeoff) currently emits raw area rows; assemblies adds a derived layer that estimators actually need.
approach: Read engine/assemblies.py to see the scaffold: what assembly spec dict it expects, what classification-to-assembly map exists

Define the assembly spec table as a Python dict: floor (area × 1.1 waste → flooring SF, CSI 09 65 00), wall_paint (perimeter × height → paint SF, CSI 09 91 23), ceiling_paint (area → paint SF, CSI 09 91 23), baseboard (perimeter → LF, CSI 06 20 00). Bathroom/kitchen also add tile SF (area, CSI 09 30 00)
Implement apply_assemblies(rooms, wall_height_ft, spec_table) → list of assembly rows. Each row: room_id, trade, csi, qty, unit
Extend build_sheet_takeoff in engine/excel.py to call apply_assemblies and write assembly rows as a new 'Assemblies' tab or inline after the room SF block
Write unit tests: bedroom (area=150, perimeter=52, height=8) → assert floor_sf=165, wall_paint_sf=416, baseboard_lf=52. Run pytest suite (expect baseline green)
resources: engine/assemblies.py — the scaffold to extend
engine/excel.py + build_sheet_takeoff — where to wire assembly rows
CSI MasterFormat: Div 09 Finishes (09 91 23 interior painting, 09 65 00 resilient flooring), Div 06 (06 20 00 finish carpentry/baseboard)
